---
title: "On Windows, install_github() can fail because of tar"
ref: ENV-05
categories: [OS and CI]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "the package installed from GitHub"
versions: "Windows, depending on the tar found in the PATH"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
remotes::install_github("ThinkR-open/golem")
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the Windows system, the tools installed in the PATH and the network, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

`install_github()` downloads a `.tar.gz` archive and unpacks it with `utils::untar()`. That function uses the program named by the `TAR` environment variable, or a `tar` found in the PATH. On Windows, several `tar` programs can live side by side (the one from Windows, from Git, from Rtools) and they do not all understand Windows paths the same way.

The extraction then fails, with an unpacking or missing-folder error that mentions neither GitHub nor the package.

## The fix

Tell R to use its internal tar implementation, which does not depend on any external program.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
Sys.setenv(TAR = "internal")
remotes::install_github("ThinkR-open/golem")
```
:::
